evidenceLimit: Primary page/text review only. No full reference-album listening or rights to reuse their recordings is claimed. Proposed lessons are our creative inferences.

sources.title: Barry Leitch: Horizon Chase and game music
sources.observed: Composer catalogue identifies the Horizon Chase releases.
sources.designInference: Use optimistic melodic motion and clearly articulated digital instruments; this is our direction, not a copied melody.

sources.title: Andrew Hulshult: game soundtrack catalogue
sources.observed: Composer catalogue lists DUSK and other game scores.
sources.designInference: Explore tension versus heavy release, distinct lead/rhythm roles and articulated guitar production.

sources.title: Mick Gordon: DOOM Behind the Music, GDC 2017
sources.observed: The composer presents creation of a high-energy modern FPS soundtrack and its franchise identity.
sources.designInference: Design original timbral experiments and rhythmic contrast; avoid copying signature DOOM riffs.

sources.title: Chris Christodoulou: Risk of Rain music
sources.observed: Composer catalogue identifies the Risk of Rain releases.
sources.designInference: Study longer-form emotional development and synth/guitar contrast during the listening phase.

sources.title: Danny Baranowsky: Super Meat Boy soundtrack
sources.observed: Composer-published soundtrack and credits are available.
sources.designInference: Use compact memorable hooks and changing energy; preserve distinct new themes.

sources.title: nervous_testpilot: Frozen Synapse
sources.observed: Artist page identifies this track as part of the Frozen Synapse soundtrack.
sources.designInference: Explore restraint, electronic space and forward pulse for menus and precision maps.

sources.title: Lena Raine: Celeste Original Soundtrack
sources.observed: Composer page credits writing, performance and mastering and lists contrasting chapter cues.
sources.designInference: Separate calm narrative/menu moments from active musical development; test motif family relationships.

sources.title: Supergiant: Hades Original Soundtrack
sources.observed: Developer-published soundtrack credits Darren Korb.
sources.designInference: Consider original acoustic/electric fusion and emotional contrast across repeated play.

sources.title: Yacht Club Games soundtrack directory
sources.observed: Developer links its official Shovel Knight releases and arranged tracks.
sources.designInference: Treat chip voice constraints as a deliberate composition approach, distinct from FM and analog synth.

sources.title: The Game Bakers: Furi
sources.observed: Official game page provides the developer source for this additional soundtrack reference.
sources.designInference: Listening candidate for electronic high-intensity pacing; no detailed musical observation claimed from page inspection.

sources.title: Go_A: official Eurovision profile
sources.observed: Documents traditional vocal technique, Ukrainian winds and deliberate electronic/heavy-guitar combinations.
sources.designInference: Give acoustic articulation a real musical role in modern arrangements; do not copy SHUM.

sources.title: ONUKA: MOZAЇKA production notes
sources.observed: Artist describes original foley rhythms, individual song concepts and electronic memories.
sources.designInference: Use our own tactile foley and acoustic/electronic dialogue.

sources.title: DakhaBrakha: artist description
sources.observed: The group describes Ukrainian folklore combined with rhythms/instruments from other cultures.
sources.designInference: Use as a contemporary fusion reference, not a supposedly pure historical ensemble.

sources.title: Authentic Ukraine: instrumental culture
sources.observed: Ethnomusicologist-authored article distinguishes instrument functions and regional dance practices.
sources.designInference: Select regional instrumentation deliberately; do not label one scale or flute as universal Ukrainian identity.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine: Kolomyika
sources.observed: Describes a Hutsul dance in 2/4 and common sung text structure.
sources.designInference: Use a two-beat dance foundation for clearly labeled modern adaptations; tempos and motifs in our briefs are new choices.

sources.title: Encyclopedia of Ukraine: Duma
sources.observed: Describes uneven recitative periods and kobza, bandura or lira accompaniment.
sources.designInference: An instrumental metered score may be tradition-informed but is not advertised as an authentic duma.

sources.title: UNESCO: kobza and wheel lyre safeguarding
sources.observed: Documents living practitioners, guilds and apprenticeship.
sources.designInference: Performance knowledge and provenance matter alongside timbre.

sources.title: UNESCO: Dnipropetrovsk Cossack songs
sources.observed: Describes lead, upper and supporting voice entries and themes including personal relationships and war tragedy.
sources.designInference: Borrow the idea of successive original counterlines, not archive recordings or a blanket heroic-war mood.

sources.title: Polyphony Project
sources.observed: Field-recording archive documents village repertoire and allows separate listening to vocal lines.
sources.designInference: Study texture and provenance; archive access does not grant sample rights.

sources.title: Ukrainian Institute: traditional music
sources.observed: Directory identifies ShchukaRyba, Syvash Station and US Orchestra with different regional/practice emphases.
sources.designInference: Use appropriate living-practitioner references for central, southern and dance directions.

sources.title: Suspilne: Vilce spring-song recordings
sources.observed: The broadcaster identifies specific villages and collectors for spring-song performances.
sources.designInference: Attach equally specific research provenance to a spring-inspired composition; do not copy its recording.
